holidays.name: Monkey Day
holidays.description: A gleeful celebration of all things simian, from lemurs and capuchins to gorillas and chimps. People dress in monkey costumes, throw banana-themed parties, and generally monkey around in the name of primate appreciation.
holidays.origin: Created in 2000 by artist Casey Sorrow, who doodled a monkey on his University of Michigan-Flint calendar on December 14 and then convinced his friend Eric Millikin to help spread the idea. It grew through the internet into a worldwide unofficial observance.
holidays.funFact: Monkey Day began as a joke between two art students, but it now inspires fundraisers for primate conservation and has been celebrated in dozens of countries.

holidays.name: National Bouillabaisse Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the famous French fish stew by simmering up a pot of seafood, saffron, fennel, and tomatoes. It is a perfect excuse to feel fancy while eating soup.
holidays.origin: Bouillabaisse comes from the port city of Marseille, where fishermen made it from the bony rockfish that were unsellable at market. The food day is an unofficial observance that grew from the American calendar of food holidays.
holidays.funFact: The name likely comes from the Provençal words 'bolhir' (to boil) and 'abaissar' (to reduce heat), which is basically the whole recipe in two words.

holidays.name: National Free Shipping Day
holidays.description: A shopping holiday when online retailers offer free shipping with guaranteed delivery before Christmas. It is the last-minute shopper's dream and the procrastinator's holiday.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2008 by Luke Knowles, who founded the event to boost online sales for retailers, and it has been held in mid-December ever since.
holidays.funFact: The founder started it to help small online stores compete with big retailers, and it began with only a few dozen participating shops before ballooning to thousands.

holidays.name: Alabama Admission Day
holidays.description: A state observance in Alabama marking its entry into the Union as the 22nd state, with history buffs and locals taking a moment to appreciate the Heart of Dixie.
holidays.origin: Alabama was admitted to the United States on December 14, 1819, after being carved out of the Mississippi Territory.
holidays.funFact: Alabama's first state capital was Cahawba, which flooded so often that the capital was moved, and today it is an archaeological ghost town.

holidays.name: Roald Amundsen South Pole Day
holidays.description: A day for explorers and armchair adventurers to remember the moment humans first set foot at the bottom of the world. Celebrate with a frosty drink, a polar documentary, or by bundling up in far too many layers.
holidays.origin: On December 14, 1911, Norwegian explorer Roald Amundsen and his team reached the South Pole, beating Robert Falcon Scott's British expedition by about five weeks.
holidays.funFact: Amundsen's team relied on sled dogs and skis, while Scott's team used ponies and motor sledges, and the difference in approach helped decide the race.
